subject: Week of Dec 6: Scanline — wins, riskiest items, and QBR asks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Week of Dec 6: Scanline — wins, riskiest items, and QBR asks

Team — quick weekly scanline to surface the small set of things we need leadership awareness/decisions on for QBR prep. Short bullets below; would appreciate any clarifying comments by EOD Mon.

Wins
- Production latency improvements: Serving runtime kernel change reduced p50 on small-sequence workloads by ~12% in hosted region-us-west. Early telemetry looks stable.
- Dedicated onboarding: Two new Dedicated customers fully migrated this week (ACME pilot and Stellar SaaS).
- Evaluate harness: First automated quality regression checks running on the nightly canary pipeline.

Riskiest items (near-term)
1) EU cluster capacity: Week-over-week tail latency increase on model-variant A (checkpoint v2) — trending toward missed SLOs if traffic grows. Root cause likely kernel selection under longer context.
2) QBR deck readiness: Need final run-rate numbers and a clean ask slide for cost mitigation options.
3) Procurement timeline: If we want burst GPUs in Q1, purchase timeline requires decision before Dec 20.

Asks (short)
- Markus: share run-rate workbook and call out sensitivity to batching and quantization (needed by Mon EOD).
- Vanessa: coordinate with procurement and ACME contacts to validate lead times (cc'd).
- Leadership: confirm appetite for a one-time credit to offset ACME onboarding in Q1 (we should decide by Dec 15).

Attachments: [Attachment: QBR-scanline-deck-v1.pptx (pptx)]

Thanks — keeping this intentionally concise so we can action.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful. Two quick asks from my side:
1) For the EU cluster tails: can you/Markus add the specific tickets and the runbook we're using for mitigation into the QBR deck as an appendix? Execs will want the mitigations and timelines in one place.
2) Run-rate: I need the run-rate by product line (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and a conservative / base / aggressive view for Q1. Markus, can you confirm you can deliver that breakdown with the assumptions?

Also — can we add a one-slide risk heatmap showing probability vs impact for the three riskiest items (EU cluster, procurement lead time, quality regression exposure)?

Laura Bennett

> 1) EU cluster capacity: Week-over-week tail latency increase on model-variant A (checkpoint v2) — trending toward missed SLOs if traffic grows.

Attaching the run-rate workbook — base/conservative/aggressive tabs included and a short notes tab with assumptions. The EU tail looks correlated with larger batch sizes hitting a slower kernel path; we have a mitigation plan that toggles batching thresholds and forces an alternate kernel selection when sequence length > 2k. That change improves p99 in staging but needs a phasing plan for traffic routing.

Attachment: [Attachment: runrate-model-2026Q4.xlsx (xlsx)]

Numbers (quick):
- Hosted base Q1 run-rate: $1.8M/mo
- Dedicated base Q1 run-rate: $1.2M/mo
- Private base Q1 run-rate: $0.35M/mo

I can add the product-line breakdown to the deck and produce the risk heatmap slide by Mon EOD.

— Markus

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Week of Dec 6: Scanline — follow-up and action items (QBR next steps)

Folks — brief follow-up with concrete asks and owners after Markus's workbook. Moving the QBR dry-run to next week so execs have a clean pre-read.

Decisions & action list
- Deck finalization (Owner: Markus) — Markus will integrate the product-line run-rate and the one-slide risk heatmap. Deliverable: QBR-scanline-deck-v1 updated by Tue Dec 14, 9am PT.
- EU cluster mitigation (Owner: Engineering/Markus) — implement alternate kernel gating in canary and run staged rollout. Target: have canary improvement validated by Dec 15.
- Procurement check (Owner: Vanessa) — Vanessa to confirm vendor lead times and whether Acme's preferred procurement channel shortens delivery vs standard. Reach out to procure@acmecorp.com; cc'ing Joi to connect. Decision deadline: Dec 20.
- Exec dry-run (Owner: Hannah) — scheduled Fri Dec 16, 10:00–11:00 PT. Invite to follow.

Notes:
- Laura: we'll include the root-cause + short remediation appendix as you requested.
- Markus: the run-rate numbers look good; please annotate the sensitivity levers (batching, quantization) so the execs can see tradeoffs in-slide.

Attachments: [Attachment: QBR-scanline-deck-v1.pptx (updated draft)], [Attachment: runrate-model-2026Q4.xlsx]

Vanessa — can you please confirm procurement timelines by EOD Mon? Joi / procure@acmecorp.com — appreciate any quick notes on their typical GPU procurement SLA and whether they can support a Q1-accelerated shipment.

Thanks everyone — short and tactical.

— Hannah
